chunks: What Sa'd narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام was asked about a menstruating woman who sweats in a garment that she wears. He said: There is nothing upon her, unless some of her fluid or some other filth touches it; then that specific spot which was affected is to be washed.

key_terms.الْمَوْضِعُ: the specific place or spot affected
key_terms.بِعَيْنِهِ: precisely itself, meaning the exact area touched
key_terms.ثَوْبٍ: a garment or piece of clothing
key_terms.فَيُغْسَلُ: then it is to be washed
key_terms.مَائِهَا: her fluid, meaning menstrual discharge in context

ai.seo_question: Does the sweat of a menstruating woman make clothes impure in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the sweat of a menstruating woman on clothing. It states that mere sweat does not render the garment impure; only the area actually affected by menstrual fluid or another impurity must be washed.
